BFM

BFM functionality is implemented in mdio_bfm_pkg.vhd

The BFM implements the MDIO management interface of IEEE 802.3, clause 22 and clause 45. It acts either as the station management entity (STA, the bus master that drives MDC) with the mdio_sta_* procedures, or as the PHY (the addressed target) with the mdio_phy_* procedures. See Abbreviations for the abbreviations used in this document.

Signal Record

t_mdio_if

Record element

Type

Description

mdc

std_logic

Management data clock, driven by the STA.

mdio

std_logic

Management data input/output. Tri-state bus, driven by the STA and by the PHY.

Note

MDIO needs a pull-up. When only the BFM is used, add a weak pull-up in the test harness, e.g. mdio <= 'H';. The VVC can drive the pull-up itself with the entity generic GC_MDIO_PULLUP set to true, see Signals.

Methods

  • All parameters in brackets are optional.

  • mdio_sta_* procedures act as the STA, mdio_phy_* procedures act as the PHY. c22 / c45 in the name selects the clause 22 / clause 45 frame format.

  • ‘terminate_loop’ aborts a call when set to ‘1’: the bus is released and ID_TERMINATE_CMD is logged, without an alert. In an MDC high phase, an STA procedure waits for the falling edge, so MDC never gets a short high pulse.

  • Every value a procedure drives onto the bus (the addresses and the write data / register address of the STA, the read data a PHY replies with) should contain ‘0’ / ‘1’ only. A ‘Z’ or ‘H’ bit is only pulled up, a ‘-’, ‘X’ or ‘U’ bit puts an ‘X’ on the bus. Such a value is a TB_ERROR at the call (one per field), but it is still driven as given: with the TB_ERROR expected, an STA can inject undefined or undriven bits to test a PHY. A PHY replying with such bits also gets a bus contention alert for them (config.bus_contention_severity). Expected values (‘data_exp’, the expected register address and data of a PHY) are only compared, so ‘-’ (don’t care) is allowed there.

STA procedures

  • The STA generates MDC with config.sta.mdc_period (idle low between calls) and sends config.sta.preamble_length ‘1’ bits before every frame (none with config.suppress_preamble). After every frame it clocks config.sta.idle_cycles IDLE bits with MDIO released.

  • MDIO is driven config.output_delay after the rising MDC edge. IEEE 802.3 22.3.4 requires the STA to hold MDIO at least 10 ns, so config.output_delay must be greater than 0 ns.

  • The target is a parameter of every call (‘phy_addr’, and ‘dev_addr’ for clause 45), as an STA talks to several PHYs and MMDs.

  • The STA never waits for the PHY, so there is no timeout parameter.

PHY procedures

Important

The BFM does not model registers or the clause 45 address register: the testbench decides what is expected or returned.

  • The address of the PHY is config.phy.phy_address. One PHY address is served by one caller (one VVC), which handles all its MMDs: several callers on the same address would take each other’s frames.

  • A call waits for the next valid frame that addresses this PHY: at least 32 preamble ‘1’ bits followed by ST, so a call may start in the middle of other traffic (config.sync_to_frame_start). Frames to other PHYs are skipped, their turnaround is checked. A read to an address without a PHY (e.g. the STA scans the bus) is not reported.

  • The addressed frame is taken whatever its clause and DEVAD. A frame of the other clause, or a clause 45 frame to another MMD than ‘dev_addr’, is reported with ‘alert_level’. A frame of the other clause is consumed without driving the bus, a frame to another MMD is handled like the expected one (e.g. a read is replied).

  • With config.sync_to_frame_start = false, the preamble is the ‘1’ bits the STA drives before ST; idle or only pulled-up (‘H’) bits are not counted.

  • The ‘timeout’ applies until the addressed frame starts, a started frame is always completed.

  • The *_receive_* procedures make the same checks as the *_expect_* procedures, but return the 16 bits the STA sent instead of comparing them.

Note

The PHY samples MDIO at the rising MDC edge. A zero-delay RTL STA that changes MDIO in the same delta cycle as MDC is out of specification (0 ns hold time) and is not received correctly. The bus timing checker of the VVC reports it.

mdio_sta_c22_write()

Writes ‘data’ to register ‘reg_addr’ of the PHY ‘phy_addr’ with a clause 22 write frame. For protocol details, see Additional Documentation.

The procedure reports an alert if:

  • A bit driven by the STA does not show on the bus, or the bus is not released after the frame (config.bus_contention_severity).

  • The configured timing violates the min_* settings of the config (config.timing_violation_severity).

  • ‘phy_addr’, ‘reg_addr’ or ‘data’ contain bits other than ‘0’ / ‘1’ (TB_ERROR, one per field). The value is still driven as given.

  • config.sta.mdc_period is not greater than 0 ns (TB_FAILURE).

  • config.output_delay is not greater than 0 ns (TB_FAILURE).

  • config.output_delay is not shorter than config.sta.mdc_period (TB_FAILURE).

mdio_sta_c22_read()

Reads register ‘reg_addr’ of the PHY ‘phy_addr’ with a clause 22 read frame and returns the data in ‘data’. ‘data’ is set to all ‘X’ at the start of the call and only assigned after a complete frame.

The procedure reports an alert if:

  • A bit driven by the STA does not show on the bus, or the bus is not released after the frame (config.bus_contention_severity).

  • The first turnaround bit is not released, i.e. is driven by someone (config.bus_contention_severity).

  • The PHY does not drive ‘0’ in the second turnaround bit (config.sta.turnaround_not_driven_severity), e.g. no PHY at that address. The data is still returned, typically all ones, so this check can be disabled to scan for PHYs.

  • The read data contains undefined bits (config.protocol_error_severity). ‘H’ and ‘L’ count as ‘1’ and ‘0’.

  • The PHY drove the second turnaround bit, but read data bits are only pulled (‘H’ / ‘L’) (config.undriven_severity). The data is still returned and compared.

  • The configured timing violates the min_* settings of the config, or config.sta.mdc_period is below 300 ns + config.min_setup_time (config.timing_violation_severity).

  • ‘phy_addr’ or ‘reg_addr’ contain bits other than ‘0’ / ‘1’ (TB_ERROR, one per field). The value is still driven as given.

  • config.sta.mdc_period is not greater than 0 ns (TB_FAILURE).

  • config.output_delay is not greater than 0 ns (TB_FAILURE).

  • config.output_delay is not shorter than config.sta.mdc_period (TB_FAILURE).

mdio_sta_c22_check()

Reads register ‘reg_addr’ of the PHY ‘phy_addr’, using the read procedure as described in mdio_sta_c22_read(). After receiving data, the data is compared with the expected data.

  • If the check was successful, and the read data matches the expected data, a log message is written with ID ‘config.id_for_bfm’.

  • If the read data did not match the expected data, an alert with severity ‘alert_level’ will be reported.

  • The data is only compared if the turnaround and the data bits were fine, otherwise that alert is reported instead of a misleading data mismatch.

  • The procedure will report alerts for the same conditions as the mdio_sta_c22_read() procedure.

mdio_sta_c45_address()

Sends a clause 45 address frame: sets the register address of the MMD ‘dev_addr’ in the PHY ‘phy_addr’ to ‘reg_addr’. The following write and read frames to this MMD access that register address.

The overload with the ‘success’ output returns false if the frame was terminated, an argument had bits other than ‘0’ / ‘1’ (TB_ERROR), or a bus check of the frame failed: a bit driven by the STA did not show on the bus, or the bus was not released after the frame (config.bus_contention_severity). A caller can then skip the access frame that would follow. Alerts from the timing check of the configuration (config.timing_violation_severity) do not set ‘success’ to false, and a check disabled with NO_ALERT counts as passed. The VVC uses it for the *_reg methods.

The procedure reports an alert if:

  • A bit driven by the STA does not show on the bus, or the bus is not released after the frame (config.bus_contention_severity).

  • The configured timing violates the min_* settings of the config (config.timing_violation_severity).

  • ‘phy_addr’, ‘dev_addr’ or ‘reg_addr’ contain bits other than ‘0’ / ‘1’ (TB_ERROR, one per field). The value is still driven as given.

  • config.sta.mdc_period is not greater than 0 ns (TB_FAILURE).

  • config.output_delay is not greater than 0 ns (TB_FAILURE).

  • config.output_delay is not shorter than config.sta.mdc_period (TB_FAILURE).

mdio_sta_c45_write()

Writes ‘data’ to the register at the current address of the MMD ‘dev_addr’ in the PHY ‘phy_addr’ with a clause 45 write frame. The register address is set with mdio_sta_c45_address() before.

The procedure reports an alert if:

  • A bit driven by the STA does not show on the bus, or the bus is not released after the frame (config.bus_contention_severity).

  • The configured timing violates the min_* settings of the config (config.timing_violation_severity).

  • ‘phy_addr’, ‘dev_addr’ or ‘data’ contain bits other than ‘0’ / ‘1’ (TB_ERROR, one per field). The value is still driven as given.

  • config.sta.mdc_period is not greater than 0 ns (TB_FAILURE).

  • config.output_delay is not greater than 0 ns (TB_FAILURE).

  • config.output_delay is not shorter than config.sta.mdc_period (TB_FAILURE).

mdio_sta_c45_read()

Reads the register at the current address of the MMD ‘dev_addr’ in the PHY ‘phy_addr’ with a clause 45 read frame and returns the data in ‘data’. The register address is set with mdio_sta_c45_address() before. ‘data’ is set to all ‘X’ at the start of the call and only assigned after a complete frame.

The procedure reports an alert if:

  • A bit driven by the STA does not show on the bus, or the bus is not released after the frame (config.bus_contention_severity).

  • The first turnaround bit is not released, i.e. is driven by someone (config.bus_contention_severity).

  • The PHY does not drive ‘0’ in the second turnaround bit (config.sta.turnaround_not_driven_severity), e.g. no PHY at that address. The data is still returned, typically all ones, so this check can be disabled to scan for PHYs.

  • The read data contains undefined bits (config.protocol_error_severity). ‘H’ and ‘L’ count as ‘1’ and ‘0’.

  • The PHY drove the second turnaround bit, but read data bits are only pulled (‘H’ / ‘L’) (config.undriven_severity). The data is still returned and compared.

  • The configured timing violates the min_* settings of the config, or config.sta.mdc_period is below 300 ns + config.min_setup_time (config.timing_violation_severity).

  • ‘phy_addr’ or ‘dev_addr’ contain bits other than ‘0’ / ‘1’ (TB_ERROR, one per field). The value is still driven as given.

  • config.sta.mdc_period is not greater than 0 ns (TB_FAILURE).

  • config.output_delay is not greater than 0 ns (TB_FAILURE).

  • config.output_delay is not shorter than config.sta.mdc_period (TB_FAILURE).

mdio_sta_c45_check()

Reads the register at the current address of the MMD ‘dev_addr’, using the read procedure as described in mdio_sta_c45_read(). After receiving data, the data is compared with the expected data.

  • If the check was successful, and the read data matches the expected data, a log message is written with ID ‘config.id_for_bfm’.

  • If the read data did not match the expected data, an alert with severity ‘alert_level’ will be reported.

  • The data is only compared if the turnaround and the data bits were fine, otherwise that alert is reported instead of a misleading data mismatch.

  • The procedure will report alerts for the same conditions as the mdio_sta_c45_read() procedure.

mdio_phy_c22_expect_write()

Waits for a clause 22 write frame to register ‘reg_addr’ of this PHY (config.phy.phy_address) and compares the written data with ‘data’. If the data matches, a log message is written with ID ‘config.id_for_bfm’. For protocol details, see Additional Documentation.

The procedure reports an alert if:

  • No addressed frame starts within ‘timeout’ (config.phy.timeout_severity).

  • MDC does not change within config.phy.max_wait_mdc_change during a frame (config.phy.max_wait_mdc_change_severity).

  • The addressed frame has the wrong clause (ST), DEVAD (clause 45), opcode, register address (clause 22) or data (‘alert_level’).

  • ST, OP, address fields or the written data contain undefined bits, the turnaround of a write or address frame is not “10”, or the STA drives fewer than 32 preamble bits (config.protocol_error_severity).

  • Preamble, ST, OP, address fields, the turnaround of a write or address frame or the written data are only pulled (‘H’ / ‘L’) instead of driven by the STA (config.undriven_severity). The data is still compared.

  • With config.suppress_preamble and config.sync_to_frame_start = false, the first bit is not the ‘0’ of ST (config.protocol_error_severity). The call ends.

  • In a frame to another target, the preamble, ST / OP / address field and turnaround checks above also apply. In a read to another target, turnaround bit 1 is driven (config.bus_contention_severity), or turnaround bit 0 is neither ‘0’ nor undriven (config.protocol_error_severity).

  • ‘timeout’ is negative (TB_FAILURE). The call returns without waiting.

  • config.phy.max_wait_mdc_change is negative (TB_FAILURE). The call returns without waiting.

mdio_phy_c22_reply_read()

Waits for a clause 22 read frame of register ‘reg_addr’ of this PHY and returns ‘data’ to the STA. MDIO is driven config.output_delay after the rising MDC edge.

The procedure reports an alert if:

  • No addressed frame starts within ‘timeout’ (config.phy.timeout_severity).

  • MDC does not change within config.phy.max_wait_mdc_change during a frame (config.phy.max_wait_mdc_change_severity).

  • The addressed frame has the wrong clause (ST), DEVAD (clause 45), opcode or register address (clause 22) (‘alert_level’).

  • ST, OP or address fields contain undefined bits, or the STA drives fewer than 32 preamble bits (config.protocol_error_severity).

  • Preamble, ST, OP or address fields are only pulled (‘H’ / ‘L’) instead of driven by the STA (config.undriven_severity).

  • The STA does not release the first turnaround bit, or the bus does not show the bits driven by the PHY (config.bus_contention_severity).

  • config.output_delay is above 300 ns (config.timing_violation_severity).

  • With config.suppress_preamble and config.sync_to_frame_start = false, the first bit is not the ‘0’ of ST (config.protocol_error_severity). The call ends.

  • In a frame to another target, the preamble and ST / OP / address field checks above also apply. In a write or address frame to another target, the turnaround is not “10” (config.protocol_error_severity) or only pulled (config.undriven_severity). In a read to another target, turnaround bit 1 is driven (config.bus_contention_severity), or turnaround bit 0 is neither ‘0’ nor undriven (config.protocol_error_severity).

  • ‘timeout’ is negative (TB_FAILURE). The call returns without waiting.

  • config.phy.max_wait_mdc_change is negative (TB_FAILURE). The call returns without waiting.

  • config.output_delay is negative (TB_FAILURE).

  • config.output_delay is not shorter than config.min_mdc_period (TB_FAILURE).

  • ‘data’ contains bits other than ‘0’ / ‘1’ (TB_ERROR). It is still driven as given, so those bits also get a bus contention alert.

mdio_phy_c45_receive_address()

Waits for a clause 45 address frame to the MMD ‘dev_addr’ of this PHY and returns the received register address in ‘reg_addr’. ‘reg_addr’ is set to all ‘X’ at the start of the call and only assigned once the address was received with the right opcode.

The procedure will report alerts for the same conditions as the mdio_phy_c22_expect_write() procedure. An address mismatch is not possible.

init_mdio_if_signals()

Initializes the MDIO interface. MDC and MDIO are set to ‘Z’ (released).

t_mdio_if := init_mdio_if_signals

-- Examples:
mdio_if <= init_mdio_if_signals;

mdio_check_bit_timing()

Passive timing check of one bit time, used by the bus timing checker of the VVC (see Bus Timing Checker). It waits for the next rising MDC edge and returns the sampled bit. The caller follows the frames and passes who drives MDIO in this bit time (‘driver’). Only the side of the bus selected with ‘checked_side’ is checked, a violation is reported with ‘alert_level’:

  • STA side (CHECK_STA or CHECK_BOTH):

    • STA_DRIVES: MDIO does not change at the rising MDC edge that starts the bit time (0 ns hold time) or within config.min_hold_time after it, and is stable config.min_setup_time before the next rising edge.

    • STA_RELEASES: hold time only, as nobody drives the next bit.

    • PHY_RELEASES: the next bit, driven by the STA, is stable config.min_setup_time before the next rising edge.

    • The MDC period between two rising and between two falling edges (config.min_mdc_period), the high time (config.min_mdc_high_time) and the low time (config.min_mdc_low_time). This is also checked with NOT_CHECKED.

  • PHY side (CHECK_PHY or CHECK_BOTH):

    • PHY_DRIVES: MDIO has settled at most 300 ns after the rising MDC edge that starts the bit time.

    • PHY_RELEASES: the PHY releases MDIO at most 300 ns after the rising MDC edge of the last data bit of a read.

With NOT_CHECKED (e.g. before the first MDC edge, or in the turnaround and data of a frame with an undefined ST/OP combination) MDIO is not checked.

mdio_check_bit_timing(mdio_if, driver, mdc_edges, sampled, checked_side, [alert_level, [scope, [msg_id_panel, [config]]]])

Local BFM overloads

A good approach for better readability and maintainability is to make simple, local overloads for the BFM procedures in the TB process. This allows calling the BFM procedures with the key parameters only, e.g.

mdio_sta_c22_write(C_PHY_ADDR, C_REG_CONTROL, x"1340", "Restart autonegotiation");

rather than

mdio_sta_c22_write(C_PHY_ADDR, C_REG_CONTROL, x"1340", "Restart autonegotiation", mdio_if, terminate_loop, C_SCOPE,
                   shared_msg_id_panel, C_MDIO_CONFIG_LOCAL);

By defining the local overload as e.g.

procedure mdio_sta_c22_write(
  constant phy_addr : in unsigned;
  constant reg_addr : in unsigned;
  constant data     : in std_ulogic_vector;
  constant msg      : in string) is
begin
  mdio_sta_c22_write(phy_addr,             -- Keep as is
                     reg_addr,             -- Keep as is
                     data,                 -- Keep as is
                     msg,                  -- Keep as is
                     mdio_if,              -- Signal must be visible in local process scope
                     terminate_loop,       -- Signal must be visible in local process scope
                     C_SCOPE,              -- Use the default
                     shared_msg_id_panel,  -- Use global, shared msg_id_panel
                     C_MDIO_CONFIG_LOCAL); -- Use locally defined configuration or C_MDIO_BFM_CONFIG_DEFAULT
end procedure;

Using a local overload like this also allows the following – if wanted:

  • Have address value as natural – and convert in the overload

  • Set up defaults for constants. May be different for two overloads of the same BFM

  • Apply dedicated message ID panel to allow dedicated verbosity control

Local BFM configuration

The default BFM configuration C_MDIO_BFM_CONFIG_DEFAULT follows IEEE 802.3 and can be used as is. A local configuration is needed to e.g. change the MDC period, the address of the PHY or to suppress the preamble.

Defining a local MDIO BFM configuration:

constant C_MDIO_CONFIG_LOCAL : t_mdio_bfm_config := (
  min_setup_time            => 10 ns,
  min_hold_time             => 10 ns,
  min_mdc_period            => 400 ns,
  min_mdc_high_time         => 160 ns,
  min_mdc_low_time          => 160 ns,
  output_delay              => 150 ns,
  id_for_bfm                => ID_BFM,
  id_for_bfm_wait           => ID_BFM_WAIT,
  suppress_preamble         => false,
  sync_to_frame_start       => true,
  protocol_error_severity   => ERROR,
  undriven_severity         => ERROR,
  bus_contention_severity   => ERROR,
  timing_violation_severity => ERROR,
  phy                       => (phy_address                  => 5x"03",
                                max_wait_mdc_change          => 1 ms,
                                max_wait_mdc_change_severity => FAILURE,
                                timeout                      => 10 ms,
                                timeout_severity             => ERROR),
  sta                       => (mdc_period                     => 1 us,
                                preamble_length                => 32,
                                idle_cycles                    => 1,
                                turnaround_not_driven_severity => ERROR)
);

The local configuration can also be derived from the default, e.g.

variable v_mdio_config : t_mdio_bfm_config := C_MDIO_BFM_CONFIG_DEFAULT;
...
v_mdio_config.sta.mdc_period    := 1 us;
v_mdio_config.phy.phy_address   := 5x"03";
v_mdio_config.suppress_preamble := true;

Compilation

  • This BFM package may only be compiled with VHDL-2008 or newer. It is dependent on the Utility Library, which is only compatible with VHDL-2008 or newer.

  • After UVVM-Util has been compiled, the BFM package can be compiled into any desired library.

  • See Essential Mechanisms - Compile Scripts for information about compile scripts.

Simulator compatibility and setup

  • See Prerequisites for a list of supported simulators.

  • For required simulator setup see UVVM-Util Simulator compatibility and setup.

Additional Documentation

For additional documentation on the MDIO protocol, please see IEEE Std 802.3, clause 22 (22.2.4 “Management functions”, 22.3.4 “MDIO timing”) and clause 45 (“Management Data Input/Output (MDIO) Interface”).

Important

  • This BFM implements the MDIO management interface of IEEE 802.3, clause 22 and clause 45, for the STA and the PHY.

  • The BFM is not a complete MDIO protocol checker, only the listed checks are made.

Abbreviations

Abbreviation

Meaning

STA

Station management entity: the bus master, drives MDC and starts every frame

PHY

The addressed target. In clause 45 any port addressed by PRTAD.

MMD

MDIO manageable device: a clause 45 device within a PHY, addressed by DEVAD

PHYAD / PRTAD

5-bit PHY / port address (clause 22 / clause 45), parameter phy_addr

DEVAD

5-bit MMD address (clause 45), parameter dev_addr

REGAD

5-bit register address (clause 22), parameter reg_addr

ST / OP / TA

Start of frame, operation code and turnaround fields of a frame

VVC

  • VVC functionality is implemented in mdio_vvc.vhd

  • For general information see VVC Mechanisms and Features.

  • The generic constant GC_STA_MODE selects the role: in STA mode the VVC drives MDC and the frames (mdio_sta_* methods), in PHY mode it answers frames from a DUT that is the STA (mdio_phy_* methods).

A VVC in STA mode drives MDC low from the start of the simulation, a VVC in PHY mode never drives MDC.

Note

MDIO needs a pull-up. Either set the generic GC_MDIO_PULLUP to true, so that the VVC drives a weak pull-up (‘H’) on mdio (in both modes), or provide the pull-up in the test harness, e.g. mdio <= 'H';. It is enough to enable the pull-up on one VVC connected to the bus.

The configuration record can be accessed from the Central Testbench Sequencer through the shared variable array, e.g.

shared_mdio_vvc_config(C_VVC_IDX).bfm_config.sta.mdc_period := 1 us;

Status Record

vvc_status accessible via shared_mdio_vvc_status

The current status of the VVC can be retrieved during simulation. This is achieved by reading from the shared variable from the test sequencer. The record contents can be seen below:

Record element

Type

Description

current_cmd_idx

natural

Command index currently running

previous_cmd_idx

natural

Previous command index to run

pending_cmd_cnt

natural

Pending number of commands in the command queue

Methods

  • All VVC procedures are defined in vvc_methods_pkg.vhd (dedicated to this VVC).

  • See Common VVC Methods for procedures which are common to all VVCs.

  • It is also possible to send a multicast to all instances of a VVC with ALL_INSTANCES as parameter for vvc_instance_idx.

  • All parameters in brackets are optional.

  • mdio_sta_* methods can only be used in STA mode, mdio_phy_* methods only in PHY mode. A command for the other role is reported with TB_ERROR and not executed.

  • Address and data parameters are unconstrained and normalized to the widths given by the protocol. A value wider than the protocol width is only accepted if the extra bits are zero.

  • Read and receive methods store the 16-bit result for fetch_result(), or send it to the scoreboard with TO_SB.

  • insert_delay() with a number of clock cycles: STA mode delays that number of bfm_config.sta.mdc_period, PHY mode waits for that number of rising MDC edges on the bus. In PHY mode MDC is driven by the DUT (STA) and usually only runs during frames, so there is no timeout: if the STA stops MDC, the delay only ends with terminate_current_command(). Use insert_delay() with a time if the DUT may stop MDC, and a timeout in await_completion() to detect a stuck VVC.

Note

Some parameters in the VVC procedures are unconstrained for flexibility. However, the maximum sizes of such parameters need to be defined for the VVC framework. For this VVC, the following maximum values can be configured from adaptations_pkg:

C_MDIO_VVC_CMD_STRING_MAX_LENGTH

Maximum msg length

mdio_sta_c22_read()

Adds a clause 22 read command to the MDIO VVC executor queue, which will run as soon as all preceding commands have completed. When the command is scheduled to run, the executor calls the BFM mdio_sta_c22_read() procedure.

The read data will not be returned in this procedure call since it is non-blocking for the sequencer/caller, but the read data will be stored in the VVC for a potential future fetch (see example with fetch_result below). If the data_routing is set to TO_SB, the read data will be sent to the MDIO VVC dedicated scoreboard where it will be checked against the expected value (provided by the testbench). This procedure can only be called when the MDIO VVC is instantiated in STA mode, i.e. setting the VVC entity generic constant ‘GC_STA_MODE’ to ‘true’.

mdio_sta_c22_check()

Adds a clause 22 check command to the MDIO VVC executor queue, which will run as soon as all preceding commands have completed. When the command is scheduled to run, the executor calls the BFM mdio_sta_c22_check() procedure. The mdio_sta_c22_check() procedure will perform a read operation, then check if the read data is equal to the expected data in the data_exp parameter. If the read data is not equal to the expected data parameter, an alert with severity ‘alert_level’ will be issued. The read data will not be stored by this procedure. This procedure can only be called when the MDIO VVC is instantiated in STA mode, i.e. setting the VVC entity generic constant ‘GC_STA_MODE’ to ‘true’.

mdio_sta_c45_write_reg()

Adds a complete clause 45 register write as one command to the MDIO VVC executor queue, which will run as soon as all preceding commands have completed. When the command is scheduled to run, the executor calls the BFM mdio_sta_c45_address() procedure followed by the BFM mdio_sta_c45_write() procedure. If the address frame fails, i.e. it is terminated or a bus check of the frame fails (bfm_config.bus_contention_severity), the access frame is not sent and the command ends. Timing alerts of the configuration (bfm_config.timing_violation_severity) do not stop the access frame. This procedure can only be called when the MDIO VVC is instantiated in STA mode, i.e. setting the VVC entity generic constant ‘GC_STA_MODE’ to ‘true’.

mdio_sta_c45_read_reg()

Adds a complete clause 45 register read as one command to the MDIO VVC executor queue, which will run as soon as all preceding commands have completed. When the command is scheduled to run, the executor calls the BFM mdio_sta_c45_address() procedure followed by the BFM mdio_sta_c45_read() procedure. If the address frame fails, i.e. it is terminated or a bus check of the frame fails (bfm_config.bus_contention_severity), the access frame is not sent and the command ends: the read returns no data (‘X’). The read data will not be returned in this procedure call since it is non-blocking for the sequencer/caller, but the read data will be stored in the VVC for a potential future fetch (see example with fetch_result below). If the data_routing is set to TO_SB, the read data will be sent to the MDIO VVC dedicated scoreboard where it will be checked against the expected value (provided by the testbench). This procedure can only be called when the MDIO VVC is instantiated in STA mode, i.e. setting the VVC entity generic constant ‘GC_STA_MODE’ to ‘true’.

t_vvc_result is defined in the corresponding vvc_cmd_pkg.vhd for the VIP.

mdio_sta_c45_check_reg()

Adds a complete clause 45 register check as one command to the MDIO VVC executor queue, which will run as soon as all preceding commands have completed. When the command is scheduled to run, the executor calls the BFM mdio_sta_c45_address() procedure followed by the BFM mdio_sta_c45_check() procedure. If the address frame fails, i.e. it is terminated or a bus check of the frame fails (bfm_config.bus_contention_severity), the access frame is not sent and the command ends. Timing alerts of the configuration (bfm_config.timing_violation_severity) do not stop the access frame. If the read data is not equal to the expected data parameter, an alert with severity ‘alert_level’ will be issued. This procedure can only be called when the MDIO VVC is instantiated in STA mode, i.e. setting the VVC entity generic constant ‘GC_STA_MODE’ to ‘true’.

mdio_sta_c45_check_reg(VVCT, vvc_instance_idx, phy_addr, dev_addr, reg_addr, data_exp, msg, [alert_level, [scope]])

mdio_phy_c22_receive_write()

Adds a clause 22 receive write command to the MDIO VVC executor queue, which will run as soon as all preceding commands have completed. When the command is scheduled to run, the executor calls the BFM mdio_phy_c22_receive_write() procedure.

The received data will not be returned in this procedure call since it is non-blocking for the sequencer/caller, but the received data will be stored in the VVC for a potential future fetch (see example with fetch_result below). If the data_routing is set to TO_SB, the received data will be sent to the MDIO VVC dedicated scoreboard where it will be checked against the expected value (provided by the testbench). This procedure can only be called when the MDIO VVC is instantiated in PHY mode, i.e. setting the VVC entity generic constant ‘GC_STA_MODE’ to ‘false’.

mdio_phy_c45_expect_write_reg()

Adds a clause 45 expect write register command to the MDIO VVC executor queue, which will run as soon as all preceding commands have completed. The command is a complete register access, the counterpart of the STA’s *_reg commands: when it is scheduled to run, the executor calls the BFM mdio_phy_c45_expect_address() procedure for the address frame, then the BFM mdio_phy_c45_expect_write() procedure for the access frame. The access frame is awaited once an address frame was received, also with a wrong DEVAD or register address (reported, the STA sends the access frame anyway). If no address frame was received (timeout, terminated, wrong clause or opcode), the command ends without waiting for the access frame. This procedure can only be called when the MDIO VVC is instantiated in PHY mode, i.e. setting the VVC entity generic constant ‘GC_STA_MODE’ to ‘false’.

mdio_phy_c45_expect_write_reg(VVCT, vvc_instance_idx, dev_addr, reg_addr, data, msg, [timeout, [alert_level, [scope]]])

mdio_phy_c45_expect_write_reg(MDIO_VVCT, 1, 5x"03", x"0000", x"2040", "Expect PCS control register write");

mdio_phy_c45_receive_write_reg()

Adds a clause 45 receive write register command to the MDIO VVC executor queue, which will run as soon as all preceding commands have completed. The command is a complete register access, the counterpart of the STA’s *_reg commands: when it is scheduled to run, the executor calls the BFM mdio_phy_c45_expect_address() procedure for the address frame, then the BFM mdio_phy_c45_receive_write() procedure for the access frame. The access frame is awaited once an address frame was received, also with a wrong DEVAD or register address (reported, the STA sends the access frame anyway). If no address frame was received (timeout, terminated, wrong clause or opcode), the command ends without waiting for the access frame. This procedure can only be called when the MDIO VVC is instantiated in PHY mode, i.e. setting the VVC entity generic constant ‘GC_STA_MODE’ to ‘false’.

The data received in the write frame will not be returned in this procedure call since it is non-blocking for the sequencer/caller, but it will be stored in the VVC for a potential future fetch (see example with fetch_result below). It is all ‘X’ if no write frame was received. If the data_routing is set to TO_SB, the received data will be sent to the MDIO VVC dedicated scoreboard where it will be checked against the expected value (provided by the testbench).

Activity Watchdog

The VVCs support a centralized VVC activity register which the activity watchdog uses to monitor the VVC activities. The VVCs will register their presence to the VVC activity register at start-up, and report when ACTIVE and INACTIVE, using dedicated VVC activity register methods, and trigger the global_trigger_vvc_activity_register signal during simulations. The activity watchdog is continuously monitoring the VVC activity register for VVC inactivity and raises an alert if no VVC activity is registered within the specified timeout period.

Include activity_watchdog(num_exp_vvc, timeout, [alert_level, [msg]]) in the testbench to start using the activity watchdog. Note that setting the exact number of expected VVCs in the VVC activity register can be omitted by setting num_exp_vvc = 0.

More information can be found in Essential Mechanisms - Activity Watchdog.

Transaction Info

This VVC supports transaction info, a UVVM concept for distributing transaction information in a controlled manner within the complete testbench environment. The transaction info may be used in many different ways, but the main purpose is to share information directly from the VVC to a DUT model.

Scoreboard

This VVC has built in Scoreboard functionality where data can be routed by setting the TO_SB parameter in supported method calls, i.e. mdio_sta_c22_read() or mdio_phy_c22_receive_write(). Note that the data is only stored in the scoreboard and not accessible with the fetch_result() method when the TO_SB parameter is applied. The MDIO scoreboard is accessible from the testbench as a shared variable mdio_vvc_sb, located in the vvc_methods_pkg.vhd, e.g.

mdio_vvc_sb.add_expected(C_MDIO_VVC_IDX, pad_mdio_sb(v_expected), "Adding expected");
mdio_sta_c22_read(MDIO_VVCT, C_MDIO_VVC_IDX, 5x"01", 5x"01", TO_SB, "Read status register");
...
mdio_vvc_sb.report_counters(ALL_INSTANCES);

The MDIO scoreboard is per default a 16 bits wide standard logic vector. When sending expected data to the scoreboard, where the data width is smaller than the default scoreboard width, we recommend zero-padding the data with the pad_mdio_sb() function, e.g.

mdio_vvc_sb.add_expected(<MDIO VVC instance number>, pad_mdio_sb(<exp data>));

pad_mdio_sb() is located in vvc_sb_support_pkg, which is not part of the MDIO vvc_context. It must be made visible in the testbench in addition to the context, e.g.

library p2l2_vip_mdio;
context p2l2_vip_mdio.vvc_context;
use p2l2_vip_mdio.vvc_sb_support_pkg.all;

A command that ends without data (terminated, timed out or wrong opcode, all reported by the BFM) sends nothing to the scoreboard and is logged with ID_DATA, the expected entry stays pending.

See the Bitvis VIP Scoreboard for a complete list of available commands and additional information. All of the listed Generic Scoreboard commands are available for the MDIO VVC scoreboard using the mdio_vvc_sb.

Unwanted Transaction Detection

This VVC supports detection of unwanted transactions from the DUT. This mechanism will give an alert if the DUT generates any unexpected bus activity that signals a transaction, e.g. asserting the valid signal. It assures that no data is output from the DUT when it is not expected, i.e. read/receive/check/expect VVC methods are not called. Once the VVC is inactive, it starts to monitor continuously on the DUT outputs. When an unwanted transaction is detected, the VVC issues an alert.

This mechanism can also monitor other signals coming from the DUT and generate alerts if any unexpected activity is detected. You can enable this by configuring the corresponding unwanted_transaction_severity for each signal you want to monitor.

The unwanted transaction detection can be configured from the central testbench sequencer, where the severity of alert can be changed to a different value. To configure this feature in the testbench, e.g.

t_mdio_unwanted_transaction

Record element

Type

Default

mdio

t_alert_level

ERROR

 
-- Disable unwanted transaction checking
shared_mdio_vvc_config(C_VVC_INDEX).unwanted_transaction_checking_enabled := FALSE;

-- Set severity of alert for the signal
shared_mdio_vvc_config(C_VVC_INDEX).unwanted_transaction_severity.mdio := WARNING;

  • STA mode: any change of mdio while the VVC is inactive is reported, except changes that keep the logic level (e.g. ‘H’ to ‘1’).

  • PHY mode: a valid frame to this PHY address that no PHY command was waiting for is reported. With the default sync_to_frame_start, the same command must be waiting from the first preamble bit to catch the frame. A waiting command takes every valid frame to this PHY address: a frame of the other clause or to another MMD is reported by the command (‘alert_level’), not as an unwanted transaction.

  • Use one PHY VVC per PHY address, also for a PHY with several MMDs: queue the commands for all MMDs on this VVC in the order the STA accesses them.

For MDIO VVC, the unwanted transaction detection is enabled by default with severity ERROR.

More information can be found in Essential Mechanisms - Unwanted Transaction Detection.

Bus Timing Checker

Every VVC runs a bus timing property checker (see Controlling Property Checkers) that follows the frames on the bus and checks every bit time with mdio_check_bit_timing(). Each mode checks the other side of the bus: PHY mode checks MDC and the bits driven by the STA, STA mode checks the bits driven by a PHY. Frames with an undefined ST/OP combination are followed to their end; only MDC is checked in their turnaround and data bits.

The checker is configured with vvc_config.bus_timing_checker and enabled with severity ERROR by default, e.g.

shared_mdio_vvc_config(C_VVC_INDEX).bus_timing_checker.enable      := false;
shared_mdio_vvc_config(C_VVC_INDEX).bus_timing_checker.alert_level := WARNING;

Compilation

The MDIO VVC must be compiled with VHDL-2008 or newer. It is dependent on the following libraries:

  • UVVM Utility Library (UVVM-Util)

  • UVVM VVC Framework

  • Bitvis VIP Scoreboard

  • MDIO BFM

Before compiling the MDIO VVC, assure that uvvm_util, uvvm_vvc_framework and bitvis_vip_scoreboard have been compiled.

See Essential Mechanisms - Compile Scripts for information about compile scripts.

Important

  • This VIP is not a complete MDIO protocol checker, only the listed checks are made.
